The corrupted WAL file has been repaired and all 11 records have been extracted to [recovered.json](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_wa8we2v/recovered.json).

### Summary of Changes
1. **Decrypted WAL File ([main.db-wal](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_wa8we2v/main.db-wal))**: Inspection of the WAL file revealed that every byte had been XOR-encoded with `0x42` (turning the WAL magic header `0x377f0682` into `0x753d44c0` and null padding bytes into `0x42`). XORing the file contents with `0x42` restored a valid SQLite WAL header and 4 valid frames with matching cumulative checksums.
2. **Extracted Complete Dataset ([recovered.json](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_wa8we2v/recovered.json))**: Using SQLite to read [main.db](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_wa8we2v/main.db) alongside the repaired [main.db-wal](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_wa8we2v/main.db-wal), we recovered all 11 records from the `items` table (including the WAL updates changing `apple` to `150` and `banana` to `250`, plus records `6` through `11`) and saved them sorted by `id` to `/app/recovered.json`.
